alerts.title: Iran Strait of Hormuz Blockade (April 13)
alerts.text: Iran announced a partial naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz Sunday evening, spiking WTI crude to $104/bbl overnight (+8%). VIX briefly touched 22 before retreating. Markets have largely digested the news as a negotiating tactic rather than a sustained closure. Energy stocks benefit directly; inflation headwind is the secondary risk for growth stocks. Monitor oil above $110 as a regime-flip trigger.

intro: 🟢 RISK-ON Continues — S&P 500 recovered to 6,886.24 (+1.02%) on Monday as markets shrugged off the Sunday night VIX spike (brief touch of ~22 on Iran blockade news). VIX closed back sub-20 for a third consecutive session. Dow is positive for 2026. The cautiously bullish regime holds.
strategy: We concentrate in the two strongest macro themes of the week: (1) Bank earnings blowout — GS already beat, JPM reports today, XLF captures the sector move; (2) Iran oil shock — COP and energy plays benefit directly from $104 WTI; (3) Defense escalation — NOC benefits from Iran geopolitics; (4) Mega-cap tech re-rotation — MSFT, ASML, SAP, TSM as AI growth names returning to favor post-ceasefire. Avoid pure domestic consumer and rate-sensitive plays until oil stabilizes.
regime_prose: The regime score stands at 0.50, classified as RISK-ON — holding from the April 10 upgrade. Component scores: SPX breadth 0.175 (bullish, above 50-DMA and 200-DMA), VIX 0.000 (sub-20 for 3+ sessions despite the Iran spike), Credit 0.850 (HYG normalizing), DXY 1.000 (dollar weak at 98.5), Liquidity 0.600, TLT 0.526. Oil spiking to $104 adds a mild inflation uncertainty penalty but does not flip the regime. Strategy weights: Momentum 50%, Breakout 30%, Pullback 20%.

pedagogy.title: Why RISK-ON despite the Iran Blockade?
pedagogy.content: The Iran Strait of Hormuz blockade is a geopolitical shock, not a structural economic shift. Markets have seen this playbook before: an oil spike, a brief VIX jump, then absorption as the situation either de-escalates or gets priced in. The key distinction is VIX behavior: Sunday night it briefly touched 22, but Monday’s session saw it retreat firmly below 20. This is the regime signal we track — not the intraday noise, but the closing behavior. Three consecutive sub-20 closes means institutional volatility sellers are dominant and the fear premium is being systematically removed. The Iran situation changes our sector allocation (more energy, more defense, less pure domestic consumer) but it does not flip the regime. RISK-ON with adjusted sector weights is the correct posture.

macro_thesis: Two powerful narratives converge this week: (1) Bank earnings season — Goldman blowout ($17.55 EPS) sets the tone. JPMorgan reports today. WFC, Citigroup, Morgan Stanley, and BofA all report by Wednesday. If the pattern holds (high FICC volatility revenues from Iran + ceasefire repositioning), financials are the cleanest RISK-ON trade of the week. (2) Iran oil shock — $104 WTI is a direct tailwind for E&P companies like COP, and a defense escalation bid for NOC. These two themes define Monday’s positioning. MSFT, ASML, SAP, TSM are the mega-cap tech/semi backbone: high-quality momentum names that benefit from dollar weakness and global AI capex without being directly exposed to the Iran oil narrative. XLF and XLI provide portfolio-level sector beta exposure to capture the thematic moves without single-stock binary risk.

setups.name: The Goldman Sachs Group
setups.description: Investment Banking / FICC / Asset Mgmt • NYSE • ~$195B mcap
setups.thesis: Goldman Sachs is the highest-conviction setup for Monday following its Q1 2026 blowout: EPS $17.55 vs $14.95 est (+17.4% beat), Revenue $17.23B (+12% YoY), ROE 19.8%. FICC trading revenues surged on the Iran volatility and ceasefire repositioning. This is a post-earnings momentum play — strong beats historically produce multi-session follow-through as analyst upgrades and target raises flow in. The earnings catalyst validates the technical breakout above the prior resistance. Goldman benefits from both themes this week: bank earnings wave + Iran FICC volatility revenues. Forward PE of ~12x is historically cheap for this level of returns.

setups.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
setups.thesis: JPMorgan Chase reports Q1 2026 earnings today (April 14), making it the most anticipated catalyst of Monday’s session. Consensus expects EPS $5.45 and Revenue $49.13B. As the first major consumer bank to report (following GS’s blowout investment banking result), JPM sets the tone for the entire financial sector this week. The stock has been building a textbook base above its 50-DMA, and the GS blowout is a strong pre-announcement tailwind for sentiment. R/R of 1:2.5 is the best in the financial pack.

setups.name: Microsoft Corporation
setups.thesis: Microsoft is the anchor mega-cap tech play for Monday. The tech sector is posting 43% earnings growth in 2026 as AI monetization accelerates, and MSFT is the clearest beneficiary: Azure cloud revenue growth has re-accelerated to ~35% QoQ, Copilot AI integration is driving ARPU expansion across Microsoft 365, and the enterprise AI budget cycle is clearly accelerating. The weak dollar (DXY 98.5) is a direct tailwind for MSFT’s ~50% international revenue. The stock is above both 50-DMA and 200-DMA in a clean momentum structure.

Azure cloud revenue re-acceleration to ~35% QoQ growth; AI Copilot ARPU uplift confirmed

setups.name: ConocoPhillips
setups.thesis: ConocoPhillips is the purest energy play in the scan. WTI crude at $104 (+8% on Iran blockade) is a direct tailwind for E&P companies like COP. Every $10 increase in WTI translates to approximately $800M in incremental annual free cash flow for COP. The Iran Strait of Hormuz blockade represents the most significant geopolitical oil risk event of 2026, and COP has the strongest leverage to sustained high oil prices of any large-cap E&P. The breakout above the 52-week high is technically clean with accelerating volume.

setups.name: Northrop Grumman Corporation
setups.thesis: Northrop Grumman is the defense escalation play in this scan. The Iran partial blockade is a direct catalyst for defense budget expansion narratives and procurement acceleration. NOC specializes in B-21 Raider stealth bombers, Sentinel ICBM systems, and space/cyber defense — all mission-critical programs that benefit from heightened geopolitical tensions. The stock has been in a steady uptrend since February and the Iran escalation provides a fresh near-term catalyst. Defense stocks historically outperform for 2-3 sessions following geopolitical escalation events.

No earnings for 3+ weeks — clean technical setup without binary event risk

setups.name: ASML Holding N.V.
setups.description: Semiconductor Equipment / EUV Lithography • NASDAQ (ADR) • ~$580B mcap
setups.thesis: ASML is the monopoly supplier of EUV lithography machines, and every major fab expansion globally (TSMC, Samsung, Intel Foundry, US CHIPS Act fabs) requires ASML equipment. The company reports its Q1 order book on April 16 (Wednesday) — consensus expects €4.5B+ in new orders driven by AI chip demand. ASML is the highest-quality semiconductor equipment play in the world with no viable competitor. The weak dollar (DXY 98.5) is a tailwind for the EUR-denominated ADR. This is a setup where the AI infrastructure capex cycle is the macro driver.

The company reports Q1 2026 earnings on April 17 (Thursday) — revenue has already been pre-announced at +35% YoY driven by CoWoS advanced packaging for AI GPUs. This is a rare pre-announced blowout: the positive surprise is already de-risked. The remaining catalyst is the Q2 guidance and CoWoS capacity expansion update, which consensus expects to be bullish. TSM is the single most important company in the AI supply chain.

setups.name: Financial Select Sector SPDR
setups.description: Financials ETF (JPM, BAC, WFC, GS, MS, etc.) • NYSE Arca • ~$42B AUM

The ETF holds all major US banks: JPM (13.5%), BAC (9.2%), WFC (8.8%), GS (4.1%), MS (4.0%), among others. When GS beats and JPM is expected to beat, the entire XLF basket re-rates. The ETF’s options market is pricing a 2.8% move this week — the setup targets half that in 5 days with a clear stop below $46.80.

setups.thesis: XLI is the industrials sector ETF and the lowest-risk setup in Monday’s scan. The ETF pulled back from recent highs to the 20-day SMA, which held as support — a textbook pullback-to-support setup in an ongoing uptrend. XLI’s composition is uniquely well-suited to the current Iran narrative: its top holdings include defense and aerospace names (RTX, GE Aerospace, Honeywell) which are benefiting from Iran escalation, as well as infrastructure names (Caterpillar, Deere) benefiting from the CHIPS Act and IRA spending wave.
